groups.title: Listening
groups.instructions: You are going to listen to a woman interviewing a student about sport. Read each question and choose the correct answer. You have 1 minute and 30 seconds to look through the questions before you listen. You will listen to the passage twice only, so listen carefully. /6 x 2 = 12 points/
groups.context:
Woman: Hi, I'm from the city sports centre. We're asking young people about their sporting habits. Do you have a few minutes?
Boy: Yes, of course.
Woman: Great. What's your name?
Boy: Tom Weston. That's W-E-S-T-O-N.
Woman: And how old are you, Tom?
Boy: I'm seventeen.
Woman: What sports do you do?
Boy: Mainly running. I'm training for my first marathon in October. I also swim, and I play table tennis with my dad.
Woman: How often do you train?
Boy: Five times a week now. When I started two years ago, I only ran once a week, just for fun.
Woman: Do you go to watch sports events?
Boy: Not really. Tickets for football matches are too expensive for me, so I watch them on TV.
Woman: What do you plan to do after school?
Boy: I want to study sports science at university and become a coach.
Woman: Good luck. And what are you going to do now?
Boy: I'm going to the park to meet my running club. We do a long run every Saturday.

passages.title: Passage 1
passages.text:
Every summer, Mongolians celebrate Naadam, the country's biggest national festival. It is often called the 'three games of men' because it includes wrestling, horse racing and archery. Today, however, women also take part in archery, and girls often ride in the horse races.

The festival has a very long history. Hundreds of years ago, Naadam was a way for warriors to show their strength and skill. Later, it became a celebration held after religious ceremonies. Today, the main Naadam takes place in Ulaanbaatar every year on 11-13 July.

Horse racing is perhaps the most surprising event for visitors. The riders are children, usually between five and thirteen years old, because **they** weigh much less than adults. The races cross the open steppe over distances of up to 30 kilometres. The horses, not the riders, are the real stars, and the winning horse is <u>praised</u> in a special song.

passages.text:
Dear Uncle Bat,

Greetings from Switzerland! We 37. _________ here on Sunday after a long flight, and the mountains are even more beautiful than in the photos. Every morning we take a cable car to the top and ski down. Mom fell twice on the first day, but she's getting better!

The village is small and quiet, and our hotel has a wonderful view of the lake. Yesterday we tried cheese fondue, which is a traditional Swiss dish. Tomorrow we're going to take a train 38. _________ the mountains to a famous glacier.

We 39. _________ home next Friday. I'll bring you some Swiss chocolate!

Best wishes,
Ariunaa
